summary: Agent quickstart: streaming disconnects when app is behind reverse proxy (SSE buffered / idle timeout)
environment: prod (us-east) — customer app deployed in Kubernetes behind Nginx Ingress + corporate proxy; observed with Redwood Hosted API streaming responses
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports intermittent streaming failures when running the Quickstart “Agents” template behind a reverse proxy/ingress.
- Symptoms: stream ends early (client sees connection drop) and the app returns a 502/499 depending on proxy, even though Redwood side shows request started successfully.

Impact
- User-visible failures on agent responses when streaming is enabled.
- Most common during agent runs that include a long tool execution step (i.e., extended period with no tokens emitted).
- Customer is in evaluation; this blocks rollout behind their standard ingress/proxy.

Customer report (sanitized)
- “When using stream=true we sometimes get a broken pipe / aborted connection around 40–90s. Non-streaming works.”
- “We’re running through Nginx ingress and corporate proxy; we can’t bypass it in prod.”

Environment details
- Quickstart: Agents template (Python + FastAPI deployment)
- Network path: Browser/client -> Corporate proxy -> Nginx Ingress -> App -> Redwood Hosted API (streaming)
- Proxy defaults: buffering enabled; read timeout ~60s (customer indicated default ingress values)

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction)
1) Deploy Agents template behind Nginx Ingress with default proxy buffering on.
2) Enable streaming responses from Redwood.
3) Trigger an agent run that performs a tool call which takes ~60s (simulated by sleeping tool / slow downstream).
4) Observe client-side disconnect and Nginx logs indicating upstream prematurely closed connection or client aborted.

Observed behavior
- Client / app logs:
  - Node (TS template): "Error: aborted" / "socket hang up" / ECONNRESET
  - Python: "httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected without sending a response" or "ReadTimeout" (depending on timeout configuration)
- Nginx ingress logs (typical): upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading upstream, or client prematurely closed connection.
- Redwood request tracing: request_id shows successful start; streaming bytes stop mid-flight; server records “client closed” prior to completion in some cases.

Expected behavior
- Streaming should remain connected through the full response, including long tool execution intervals, or the template should fail gracefully and provide actionable guidance.

Initial analysis / likely cause
- The issue is consistent with reverse proxies buffering SSE or enforcing idle timeouts when no bytes are forwarded.
- Agent flows can have long gaps with no token emission while tools execute (especially if tools are network calls). Proxies often consider this an idle upstream.
- Some proxy stacks also default to HTTP/2 upstream and/or buffer chunked responses; both can break SSE unless explicitly configured.

Workaround provided to customer
A) Proxy configuration for SSE (recommended)
- Disable proxy buffering for the streaming route and increase upstream read timeout. Example Nginx directives:
  - proxy_buffering off;
  - proxy_request_buffering off;
  - proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
  - proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
  - proxy_http_version 1.1;
  - gzip off;
- If using Nginx Ingress, annotate the ingress for the streaming endpoint:
  - nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "3600"
  - nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "3600"
  - nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off"

B) Template-side mitigations (acceptable for evaluation)
- Disable streaming temporarily (stream=false) for the agent endpoint to confirm baseline functionality behind proxy.
- Reduce maximum tool execution time (tool timeout wrapper) to keep gaps shorter.

SDK update reference
- Recommended upgrading to the latest SDK helper that standardizes timeouts/retries and improves streaming error classification:
  - Python: redwood-sdk-python PR #512 (streaming retry/backoff helpers + clearer timeout defaults)
  - TypeScript: redwood-sdk-typescript PR #441 (improved error typing + trace context propagation helpers; includes better guidance for 499/502-style disconnects)
- Note: retries cannot safely resume mid-stream; the SDK update focuses on (1) preventing overly aggressive client timeouts, (2) clearer actionable errors, and (3) consistent request_id capture for Console correlation.

Resolution criteria
- Customer confirms stable streaming after disabling buffering + increasing read timeout, OR opts to ship non-streaming until their ingress policy is updated.

Follow-ups
- Add a “Behind a proxy?” section to the Agents template README with known-good ingress/proxy settings and common failure signatures.
- Consider adding optional SSE heartbeat events from template server during tool execution (would require template changes; track separately if needed).

2026-02-07 10:25 Dev Patel (Support)

They also noted the disconnect happens more often when the agent triggers a tool call that takes ~1 minute.

2026-02-07 11:11 Sean Gallagher (SRE)
This pattern is classic SSE + buffering/idle-timeouts. During tool execution there may be no bytes forwarded to the client, so ALB/ingress/proxy sees an “idle” upstream and closes.

Recommended: disable proxy buffering and set proxy_read_timeout high on the streaming route. Also keep upstream to HTTP/1.1 for SSE when possible. If they must keep buffering globally, carve out a path/host for /agent/stream.

- gzip off

Also advising to test “stream=false” as a control to confirm proxy is the differentiator.

For SDK side: we should point them to the new standardized timeout defaults in redwood-sdk-python PR #512; reduces client-side ReadTimeout confusion, but won’t fix proxy buffering by itself.

resolution: Root cause identified as reverse proxy buffering and/or idle read timeouts breaking SSE during agent tool-execution gaps (no bytes forwarded). Provided Nginx Ingress configuration to disable buffering and increase proxy_read_timeout, plus a temporary non-streaming workaround. Customer confirmed stable streaming after config changes. Pointed customer to SDK updates (redwood-sdk-python #512 / redwood-sdk-typescript #441) for improved timeout defaults and clearer streaming error classification (not a mid-stream resume mechanism).
